packages/docs-web/src/content/docs/guide: 1. **Substitute variables.** `$WORKFLOW_ID`, `$ARTIFACTS_DIR`, `$STATE_DIR`, `$ADOPTED_RUN_DIR`, `$TYPED_ARTIFACTS_FILE`, `$BASE_BRANCH`, `$DOCS_DIR`, and upstream `$nodeId.output` references are substituted into the `script` text before execution. User-controlled workflow variables like `$ARGUMENTS` and `$USER_MESSAGE` are not substituted into a `script:` body: they arrive as environment variables instead (`process.env.ARGUMENTS`, `process.env.USER_MESSAGE` in bun; `os.environ['ARGUMENTS']`, `os.environ['USER_MESSAGE']` in uv/python), so these workflow-variable values stay out of script source — see [Environment and Isolation](#environment-and-isolation). Upstream output references are still substituted as raw text into script source and may contain user-influenced content.

For **named scripts**, read workflow variables from the environment (`process.env.USER_MESSAGE`, `os.environ['USER_MESSAGE']`) and `with:` bindings from `INPUTS_<UPPER_SNAKE>` environment variables. Named scripts receive no stdin payload. For **inline scripts**, substituted variables are literally embedded into the code string at execution time.

:::note[Shell injection prevention] User-controlled workflow variables like `$USER_MESSAGE` and `$ARGUMENTS` are passed to `bash:` nodes as environment variables (not inline-substituted into the shell command) to prevent shell injection — read an environment-delivered value with `"$ARGUMENTS"`. `script:` nodes receive these values the same way (`process.env.USER_MESSAGE`, `process.env.ARGUMENTS` in bun; `os.environ['USER_MESSAGE']`, `os.environ['ARGUMENTS']` in uv/python). A `loop_group` body's `bash:` node is the exception: the loop scope splices the reply (`$LOOP_USER_INPUT`) into its source, shell-quoted, so the reply arrives already quoted. Read the spliced reply as an already-quoted value — assign it and quote the variable (`value=$LOOP_USER_INPUT; printf '%s' "$value"`) — rather than as `"$LOOP_USER_INPUT"`. :::
packages/docs-web/src/content/docs/refer: Archon substitutes variables in command files, inline prompts, bash scripts, and `script:` node bodies before execution — except the user-controlled variables, which reach `bash:` and `script:` nodes as environment variables instead. There are two categories of variables: workflow variables (substituted by the workflow engine) and node output references (DAG workflows only).

These variables are substituted by the workflow executor in all node types (`command:`, `prompt:`, `bash:`, `script:`, `loop:`, `loop_group:`, and a `workflow:` node's `input:` field — which behaves like a `prompt:` body, not a bash-escaped one) — except the user-controlled ones in `bash:` and `script:` nodes, which arrive as environment variables instead (see [Shell quoting in `bash:` vs `script:`](#shell-quoting-in-bash-vs-script)).

User-controlled variables (`$ARGUMENTS`, `$USER_MESSAGE`, `$LOOP_USER_INPUT`, `$LOOP_PREV_OUTPUT`, `$REJECTION_REASON`, `$CONTEXT` and its aliases) are delivered to `bash:` and `script:` nodes as subprocess **environment variables** (`ARGUMENTS`, `USER_MESSAGE`, `LOOP_USER_INPUT`, `LOOP_PREV_OUTPUT`, `REJECTION_REASON`, `CONTEXT`/`EXTERNAL_CONTEXT`/`ISSUE_CONTEXT`), never spliced as raw text into executable code — so attacker-influenced input can't inject. A `loop_group` body's `bash:` node is the exception: the loop scope splices the reply (`$LOOP_USER_INPUT`) into its source, shell-quoted, so the reply arrives already quoted. Read the spliced reply as an already-quoted value — assign it and quote the variable (`value=$LOOP_USER_INPUT; printf '%s' "$value"`) — rather than as `"$LOOP_USER_INPUT"`. In `bash:` read an environment-delivered value with `"$ARGUMENTS"`. In `script:` read it via `process.env.ARGUMENTS` (bun) or `os.environ['ARGUMENTS']` (uv/python). A literal `$ARGUMENTS`/`$USER_MESSAGE`/`$CONTEXT` left in a `script:` body is not substituted: the text stays in the source, so a quoted reference keeps the literal text and a bare one fails the node.

The load-time environment-read check uses these same binding names and the workflow's declared input names. For example, `process.env.INPUTS_GREEN` requires `with: { green: ... }` on that script node or a declared `green` workflow input. Engine-owned names such as `ARTIFACTS_DIR`, `BASE_BRANCH`, `ARGUMENTS`, and `WORKFLOW_ID` are always accepted.
.claude/skills/archon-cli/authoring/node: - In `bash:` and `script:` sources, user-controlled variables (`$ARGUMENTS`, `$USER_MESSAGE`, `$LOOP_USER_INPUT`, `$LOOP_PREV_OUTPUT`, `$REJECTION_REASON`, `$CONTEXT`) are **not** spliced as raw text (injection guard); they arrive as environment variables (`ARGUMENTS`, `USER_MESSAGE`, `LOOP_USER_INPUT`, `LOOP_PREV_OUTPUT`, `REJECTION_REASON`, `CONTEXT`, `EXTERNAL_CONTEXT`, `ISSUE_CONTEXT`). Read an environment-delivered value in `bash:` as `"$ARGUMENTS"`. In `script:` read it via `process.env.ARGUMENTS` (bun) or `os.environ['ARGUMENTS']` (uv/python). A `loop_group` body's `bash:` node is the exception: the loop scope splices the reply (`$LOOP_USER_INPUT`) into its source, shell-quoted, so the reply arrives already quoted. Read the spliced reply as an already-quoted value — assign it and quote the variable (`value=$LOOP_USER_INPUT; printf '%s' "$value"`) — rather than as `"$LOOP_USER_INPUT"`. `$nodeId.output` refs ARE substituted; give prose producers an `output_format` before assigning their output directly in a script.
.claude/skills/archon-cli/authoring/vari: - **`bash:` scripts** — SPECIAL: user-controlled variables (`$ARGUMENTS`, `$USER_MESSAGE`, `$LOOP_USER_INPUT`, `$LOOP_PREV_OUTPUT`, `$REJECTION_REASON`, `$CONTEXT`) are **NOT spliced as raw text** into the script (shell-injection guard). A `loop_group` body's `bash:` node is the exception: the loop scope splices the reply (`$LOOP_USER_INPUT`) into its source, shell-quoted, so the reply arrives already quoted. Read the spliced reply as an already-quoted value — assign it and quote the variable (`value=$LOOP_USER_INPUT; printf '%s' "$value"`) — rather than as `"$LOOP_USER_INPUT"`. In `bash:`, they arrive as **environment variables** instead: `ARGUMENTS`, `USER_MESSAGE`, `LOOP_USER_INPUT`, `LOOP_PREV_OUTPUT`, `REJECTION_REASON`, `CONTEXT` (+ `EXTERNAL_CONTEXT`/`ISSUE_CONTEXT`), plus `ARTIFACTS_DIR`, `LOG_DIR`, `BASE_BRANCH` — read an environment-delivered value with `"$ARGUMENTS"` as normal shell env access. `$nodeId.output` refs ARE substituted: small string values are single-quoted inline; values exceeding 32,768 UTF-16 code units (JavaScript `string.length`) spill to a file and substitute as unquoted `$(cat '<path>')`, which drops trailing newlines; the command substitution splits words and expands globs when used as a bare argument. Assign first (`value=$nodeId.output`), then quote the shell variable (`printf '%s' "$value"`) to handle both forms. See [Shell quoting guidance](https://archon.diy/reference/variables/#shell-quoting-in-bash-vs-script).

- **`script:` bodies** — like `bash:`, user-controlled variables (`$ARGUMENTS`, `$USER_MESSAGE`, `$LOOP_USER_INPUT`, `$LOOP_PREV_OUTPUT`, `$REJECTION_REASON`, `$CONTEXT`) are **NOT spliced as raw text** into the source (injection guard, #2115). They arrive as **environment variables** — `ARGUMENTS`, `USER_MESSAGE`, `LOOP_USER_INPUT`, `LOOP_PREV_OUTPUT`, `REJECTION_REASON`, `CONTEXT` (+ `EXTERNAL_CONTEXT`/`ISSUE_CONTEXT`), plus `ARTIFACTS_DIR`, `LOG_DIR`, `BASE_BRANCH` and managed per-project env — read via `process.env.ARGUMENTS` (bun) / `os.environ['ARGUMENTS']` (uv/python) — env vars are the general injection-safe channel for untrusted values. A literal `$ARGUMENTS`/`$USER_MESSAGE`/`$CONTEXT` left in the source is not substituted: the text stays in the source, so a quoted reference keeps the literal text and a bare one fails the node. `$nodeId.output` values are still substituted **raw** (not shell-quoted). Direct assignment (`const data = $nodeId.output;`) is safe **only with `runtime: bun` when the producer uses `output_format`**. JSON booleans and nulls are not Python literals, so a `runtime: uv` script should bind the value with `with: { data: "$nodeId.output" }` and parse `os.environ['INPUTS_DATA']` with `json.loads`. For arbitrary-text producers (bash/script stdout or prose), use the same environment binding instead of embedding the raw value in source, then parse defensively only if the text is expected to contain JSON. **Avoid wrapping `$nodeId.output` in a `String.raw` template literal** — it silently breaks when the output contains a backtick (common in AI-generated markdown and `output_format` payloads)

Despite older docs suggesting otherwise, positional `$1`…`$9` are **not substituted** by the workflow engine — command files and prompts receive the whole message only, via `$ARGUMENTS`/`$USER_MESSAGE`. (A legacy positional-substitution helper exists in the codebase but is not wired into the execution path.) Parse arguments inside the prompt or with a `bash:`/`script:` node instead.
